title: Trade game iteration 2: small loops built up a knot hierarchy, intermediate towns, bases anywhere, levels in .ix files, one class per game object
description:
Second iteration of the trade game after playing TRADE-23's MVP: change the rules so the fun is building small loops and combining them up a knot hierarchy, fix the feel and the interface, and restructure the code into one class per game object with level data in .ix files. Design record: obsidian `Notes/Trading Game Design.md` ("After playing the MVP") and card 10 of `Notes/Trading Game One-Page Design.html`.

Gameplay
- Point density is too low and limits too generous: every level is won by growing one mega-loop to every city. Add intermediate towns: road-connected points loops can route through, with no market (no station, no sales). Tighten wagon capacity and fuel so one loop cannot reach everything; the play becomes several small loops piped and collapsed into a hierarchy.
- Bases can be built anywhere, priced (and upkept) by distance from the true home, like EU4's free capital versus provincial seats. Drop the "dominant for 2 laps" gate, which made bases arrive only after a city was won and made the rival's side unreachable.
- Moving through the knot hierarchy is play: `[` and `]` go down and up levels as in the knot editor. Design how a pipe or collapse made at one level reacts to edits at another (open question below).

Feel
- Gold flies from each city to the gold counter with slightly randomised, high-"velocity" pickup sounds (Ratchet & Clank bolt collection). Today there is no gold sound at all.
- Direction arrows follow the Bezier lanes, and each side of a road can carry its own direction (opposite for out-and-back, same for parallel loops). Today one SDFLine arrow sits on the straight middle step of a leg and does not follow the curve. Needs a lane/arrow shader (or the arrow shader extended to curves with per-side direction).

Interface
- The bottom toolbar does not fit the half-screen F5 window: buttons must wrap, stack or scroll.
- The city panel shows even with no city selected; show the city menu only for a selected city and close it on clicking off.
- Map modes colour circles per cell; colour the cell's actual area. Moor likewise.
- Grid lines are 1 px at every zoom and aliased (fixed pixel width through SDFLine); draw them at a zoom-scaled width with the line shader. About half the boundary edges are missing because the `corners[k] < corners[k+1]` dedupe drops sides owned by one cell; draw every unique edge (`Layout.edges`).

Code (from a design review of TRADE-23, commit 8003d223)
1. Undo: `TradeGame` replays the whole operation list from fresh knots, discarding the `PipeRecord`/`GrowRecord`/`CollapseRecord` that Knot already returns, so wagons need a knot-identity workaround (`wagonsByTop`/`previousTopOfCity`), any RuntimeException reads as "would cross", and undo reaches back past a settled lap. Use `EditHistory<OperationRecord>` (a `RouteHistory`), cleared at lap end, with explicit validation that returns a refusal.
2. God classes: `TradeGame` (1174 lines) holds every concept as int-indexed parallel lists and `company == PLAYER ?` branches; `TradeScene.drawScene` is one 360-line method. One class per game object (see layout below); enums for company, outcome, price war and operation kind.
3. Data as Java: `TradeLevel.campaign()` hardcodes coordinates, demand, rivers and moors; economy tuning is constants in `TradeGame`; `TradeRivalLevelScene` exists only to pass an index. Extend the .ix format (line-oriented `KEYWORD args` records parsed in `PointSetPath.importFromFile`, primitives as `@GeometryAnnotation` classes with `parse`/`toFileString`, `LOAD` nesting, read via `Platforms.loadFile`) with trade records: `MAP`, `CITY`, `TOWN`, `RIVER`, `BRIDGE`, `MOOR`, `COMPANY`, `STATION`, `BASE`, `LOOP`, `GOAL`, `LAPS`, `TITLE`, `RULES key value`, dispatched through a keyword registry with each game-object class owning its `parse`/`toFileString`. `GENERATE <generator> <seed> <params>` calls a `TradeMapGenerator` (cities by Poisson sampling, river traced on a noise field, moor from thresholded noise) whose result can be saved as an editable .ix. Scenes take a level path; the campaign is a list of files.
4. Rivers, roads and bridges: roads are `int[]` cell paths, the river a free polyline, and a bridge is the cell pair whose midpoint height is nearest a requested y, drawn at that midpoint (not on the river, so it spans half the river when zoomed). Loop crossings are tested on straight lines between cities while lanes follow grid paths. Add `GridPath` (primal or dual node sequence with polyline, steps, `crosses`, smoothed curve); `Road`, `River` (a primal path along cell sides, blocking every dual step across them) and `Leg` are GridPaths; `Bridge(River, side)` is built from the crossed side and placed and oriented on it; crossings use `Leg.path.crosses`.
5. `TradeMap` copies the layout, and `TradeGame` builds a second anchors-only `IrregularQuadGrid`; `IrregularQuadGrid.draw` is a no-op. Build the grid once and move faces, neighbours, `edgeKey` and A* onto it as a generic grid graph; `TradeMap` only adds terrain.
6. Rendering: add `graphics/render/grid/GridRenderer` (unique edges at world-unit width times zoom, cell fills from a per-cell colour array as one buffer of triangle fans, for moor, territory and fog) and `PathRenderer` (arc-length sampling of a GridPath curve, lane offsets along the normal, dashed off-road spans, chevrons along the tangent; the lap animation reuses its sampling). Territory should use grid distance, not a Euclidean nearest-city lookup in the scene. City hit-testing uses a 20 world-unit radius while cities draw at 11 px, so clicks drift with zoom.
7. Route tools: `RoutePlanningTool` is one class switching on modes. Mirror the knot editor (`tools/knot/KnotTool` owns hover, selection, left/right cycling, `[`/`]` layer controls and Enter→confirm): an abstract `TradeRouteTool` (pending city, layer controls over the scene's knot layer, undo/redo via RouteHistory, shared overlay) and `PipeTool`, `GrowTool` (owning the grow-target preview now in TradeGame), `CollapseTool`. The toolbar lists `scene.tools`. City selection moves to the scene.
8. HUD: hardcoded x positions, button rectangles in parallel lists, inline label arrays. Add a `HudPanel` base (bounds, draw, click, own buttons) with `TopBar`, `StatusLine`, `CityPanel`, `LoopListPanel`, `Toolbar`, `OutcomeDialog`; the map side is `MapView` and `LapAnimation`; the scene keeps layout and dispatch.
9. Knot: the "remove a segment from manifold and sorted lists and unmatch both ends" block is copied six times; make it `Knot.removeSegment(Segment)`, ideally over identity-based segment lists. The ancestor patch after `grow` in `TradeGame.perform` belongs in `Knot.grow`; `top`, `childOf`, `deepestOwner` are Knot hierarchy queries.
10. Dead code: `City` population/resources/produces/consumes/draw/tooltip, all of `Road`, `CityNetwork` road generation and draw, `resources/cities/*.json`. A city lives in three places (a City, `cityCell[]`, `level.cityNames[]`) with ids round-tripped through `Integer.toString`/`parseInt`; loop rotation and path reversal are copied; magic numbers remain (half cost 0.5, HUD spacings, reserve thresholds).

Proposed layout (each class owns its data and behaviour)
- `ixdar.game.trade.map`: TradeMap, GridPath, Road, River, Bridge, TerrainRegion (moor), Town (intermediate, road junction), RouteTable (legs between points).
- `ixdar.game.trade.economy`: City, Facility (NONE/STATION/BASE with price, upkeep, production; base price by distance from home), Market, Company (+ RivalStrategy), Loop, Wagon, LapSettlement, Outcome.
- `ixdar.game.trade.routes`: RouteNetwork (knots, validated pipe/grow/collapse returning OperationRecords), RouteHistory.
- `ixdar.game.trade.level`: TradeLevel, TradeLevelFile (.ix read/write + registry), TradeMapGenerator, Rules.
- `ixdar.game.trade`: TradeGame (thin orchestration).
- `ixdar.graphics.render.grid`: GridRenderer, PathRenderer.
- `ixdar.scenes.trade`: TradeScene (takes a level path), MapView, LapAnimation, hud/*.
- `ixdar.tools.trade`: TradeRouteTool, PipeTool, GrowTool, CollapseTool.

Colours go through UI-17's named scene palettes; this ticket should not add more raw `Color` uses than it must.

User decisions after the first write-up: the city menu and the loop list are separate panels, and the city panel appears only while a city is selected. Fixed 1-px grid lines are rejected outright: grid lines scale with zoom. Every item in the 'why' list (sound, toolbar overflow, bridges, a shared river/road path class, level data in .ix) is a defect to fix in this ticket, not an explanation. One-class-per-thing rule for this ticket: a separate class for each idea with its own drawing or function (Road allows movement, River blocks it, Bridge allows it only across a river; they share one routing/drawing path class but carry different attributes); the object count here is small, so parallel arrays are not warranted. Parallel arrays stay for bulk data such as mesh edges.
definition-of-done:
1. Levels load from .ix files under resources/trade/ (with GENERATE for algorithmic maps); no level or tuning data is hardcoded in Java, and TradeRivalLevelScene is gone.
2. Intermediate towns exist on every map, are road-connected and routable but have no market; tightened capacity and fuel mean a plain "grow to every city" plan no longer wins the rival level, while a plan of several small loops piped into a hierarchy does (unit tests for both).
3. Bases can be built at any city, priced and upkept by distance from home; the dominance gate is gone.
4. `[` and `]` move down and up the knot hierarchy in the trade scene, and the documented rule for how pipes/collapses at one level react to edits at another is implemented and tested.
5. Gold flies to the gold counter at lap end with randomised pickup sounds.
6. Direction arrows follow the curved lanes, with per-side direction, via a lane/arrow shader.
7. The toolbar fits a half-screen window; the city menu appears only for a selected city and closes on clicking off; map modes and moor fill whole cells; grid lines scale with zoom and every boundary edge is drawn.
8. Code matches the proposed layout in spirit: one class per game object, GridPath shared by roads, rivers and legs, Bridge built from the crossed river side, the grid built once, GridRenderer and PathRenderer, HUD panels as objects, Pipe/Grow/Collapse as separate Tools under a TradeRouteTool base, undo through EditHistory<OperationRecord>, the Knot segment-removal block deduplicated, and the dead City/Road/CityNetwork code removed.
9. Screenshots under tmp/ show the half-screen toolbar, a selected and an unselected map, cell-filled map modes, curved arrows on an out-and-back road, and a hierarchy of piped loops at two levels.
testing-plan:
1. Unit tests: .ix round trip (parse then write yields the same level); GENERATE is deterministic per seed; a bridge sits on its river side; GridPath crossings agree with drawn lanes; undo/redo through EditHistory restores loops and wagons and stops at the last settled lap; base price grows with distance from home; the mega-loop plan loses and the small-loops plan wins the rival level.
2. Run the rival level at half-screen size with ixdar-cli launch and screenshot the toolbar; click a city then empty map and screenshot both; cycle map modes; zoom in on a bridge and on grid lines.
3. End a lap and confirm the gold animation and pickup sounds (ixdar-cli audio-log).
4. mvn -q compile is clean; the trade tests, ColorOrderTest and the full unit suite pass.

changes-made: Rebuilt the trade game as small classes: map (TradeMap, GridPath, Road, River, Bridge from a river side, Moor, Place, City, Town), economy (Company, Loop, Offer, Market, Economy, Rules), routes (Leg, RouteTable, RouteNetwork with knot layers, RouteOperation, RouteState snapshot undo), level (.ix files under resources/trade read by TradeLevelFile, maps built by TradeMapGenerator with generated towns, cities and roads). Pipe/Grow/Collapse are Tools sharing TradeRouteTool; [ and ] step the layer an edit acts inside. Bases anywhere, priced 60 + 4 per cell from home. Tanks 56-64 so one mega-loop runs dry or loses and compact loops at bases win (TradeGameTest). New SDFLane (chevrons follow the curve) and SDFPolygon (cell fills) shaders; GridRenderer draws every side once at zoom-scaled width; HUD split into TopBar, StatusLine, CityPanel (only while a city is selected), LoopListPanel, Toolbar (wraps) and OutcomeDialog; map framed into the free area. Gold flies to the counter with four synthesised clink WAVs at random pitch (AudioBackend.playSfxOnce gained a pitch). Removed the old City, Road, CityNetwork, TradeGame, TradeLevel, TradeMap, TradeMarket, RoutePlanningTool, TradeRivalLevelScene and resources/cities. Screenshots in tmp/.
